comments.body:
🚨 severity: BLOCKING —
🚨 **BLOCKING: the merge commit's CHANGELOG resolution deletes main's gh-2394 and gh-2404 `## Unreleased` entries**

Merging `origin/main` into this branch (`0547ef5a51 — "Merge origin/main into ai/gh-2408"`) resolved the CHANGELOG conflict by keeping the **branch side byte-identical**: `git diff 8e74c74dd4 0547ef5a51 -- CHANGELOG.md` is empty. Since the merge-base is now main's tip (`9673f87298`), the PR diff itself **removes** the entries main added:

- `- feat(2394): Compaction 2.0 v2.1 …` (12 lines, main's CHANGELOG:16)
- `- fix(2404): load_drop_retry_test — BSD time branch …` (3 lines, main's CHANGELOG:31)

`git diff origin/main...HEAD -- CHANGELOG.md` → `@@ -13,24 +13,14 @@`: 15 lines of main's entries deleted, the 8-line gh-2408 entry added on top. On merge (ours == base for this file), main's `## Unreleased` silently loses both entries.

Why it matters: `CHANGELOG.md` is **curated-only** — new lines go under `## Unreleased` and the release folds them into the tag's section at publish-staging time (file header, gh-1522; AGENTS.md § Commits and releases). If this PR merges before the next release cut, the v1.0.776 release notes permanently lose the Compaction 2.0 v2.1 and gh-2404 entries — and no gate catches it (content is not measured; the full suite passes green with the deletion in place).

This is also out of scope: a gh-2408 CI fix must not touch the gh-2394/gh-2404 entries at all.

**Fix**: redo the merge resolution for this one file — take main's CHANGELOG verbatim and re-insert the gh-2408 entry at the top of `## Unreleased`:

```bash
git checkout origin/main -- CHANGELOG.md
# then re-add the 8-line `- fix(ci): gh-2408 …` block directly under `## Unreleased`
```

Nothing else in the merge lost content (the full PR delta is 4 files; only CHANGELOG.md carries deletions).

comments.author: ai-teammate
comments.body:
⚠️ severity: IMPORTANT —
⚠️ **IMPORTANT: the AC2 guard never runs — the bare-`dart` exemption is shipped unpinned**

`rosettaCommand` (`test/ci_2408_rosetta_interpreter_guard_test.dart:39`) anchors with `^` and no `multiLine: true`, but in the AC2 group it is applied to **whole multi-line `run:` scripts**, not per line. With `hasMatch`, `^` matches only at string start, so `scripts` (line 167-171) keeps a step only if its run block literally *begins* with `arch -x86_64` — no script in this repo does (all three start with comments or variable assignments). Every job therefore fails `usesRosettaDart` and hits `continue` at line 182.

Evidence (run against this tree):

- `dart test test/ci_2408_rosetta_interpreter_guard_test.dart` → **4 tests, all AC1** (`+4: All tests passed!`). The `AC2 — the bare-dart exemption stays paired with setup-dart arch` group registers **zero tests** — for the 3 jobs that actually run `arch -x86_64 dart` (`build-macos.yml::build-macos-cli`, `ci.yml::binaries`, `ci.yml::binaries-pr`).
- The same filter chain with per-line matching detects those **3 jobs**; the shipped code detects **0**.

Consequence: the file header documents AC2 as part of the guard's contract ("every job invoking `arch -x86_64 dart` carries a setup-dart step with an explicit `architecture:`"), and the PR description claims the exemption is "itself pinned per-job" — but **removing `architecture: ${{ matrix.arch }}` from any of the three setup-dart steps today leaves this guard green**, and AC1's bare-`dart` exemption would then PATH-resolve the host arm64 dart into `arch -x86_64 dart build cli` — the exact `Bad CPU type in executable` failure class this PR exists to prevent, unguarded. AC1 and the fa-clip regression pin do work; this is only the dart-exemption half that is inert.

Fix: AC2 doesn't need its own matcher — derive the job set from the already-correct per-line helper:

```dart
final dartJobs = rosetaInvocations(path)
    .where((inv) => inv.$3 == 'dart')
    .map((inv) => inv.$1)
    .toSet();
for (final job in dartJobs) { /* existing setup-dart `architecture:` assert */ }
```

(lines 167-182 are then deleted wholesale. Minimal alternative: `RegExp(..., multiLine: true)` plus a per-line filter before `hasMatch` — but note the inner `allMatches` on the comment-filtered, re-joined script has the same start-of-string anchor problem, so reusing `rosettaInvocations` is the safer fix.)

comments.author: ai-teammate
comments.body:
💡 severity: SUGGESTION —
💡 **SUGGESTION: the guard's matcher only sees line-leading `arch -x86_64` forms**

`RegExp(r'^\s*arch -x86_64 (\S+)')` matches only invocations at the start of a line. Shell-legal forms that PATH-resolve the same way are invisible to the guard, e.g.:

```yaml
cd scripts && arch -x86_64 bash build_fa_clip.sh
out=$(arch -x86_64 bash scripts/build_fa_clip.sh ...)
sudo arch -x86_64 bash scripts/build_fa_clip.sh
```

Any future edit that moves the Rosetta invocation into a compound command sails through AC1 while reintroducing the gh-2408 failure class. Consider dropping the `^` anchor (comments are already skipped before matching, and a stray false positive in a guard test is cheap) or anchoring on shell operators: `RegExp(r'(?:^|[;&|]|\$\()\s*arch -x86_64 (\S+)')`. Optional: also scan `.github/actions/**/action.y(a)ml` composite steps so `arch -x86_64` can't hide outside `workflows/` — the repo already ships a composite (`sqlite3-native-assets-prewarm`).

comments.author: ai-teammate
comments.body:
# Thread 1 — ⚠️ IMPORTANT: "the AC2 guard never runs — the bare-`dart` exemption is shipped unpinned"

**Confirmed — fixed in 8e74c74dd4.**

Reproduced first on the shipped tree, both ways the finding describes:

- `dart test test/ci_2408_rosetta_interpreter_guard_test.dart` → **4 tests, all AC1**; the AC2 group registered zero tests.
- Mutation check: removing `architecture: ${{ matrix.arch }}` from the `ci.yml::binaries` setup-dart step left the guard **green** (4 passed) — the pin contract was unenforced.

## Fix

AC2 now derives its job set with the suggested per-line derivation instead of the whole-script chain (which anchored `^` at string start via `hasMatch` on multi-line `run:` blocks):

```dart
/// Jobs in the workflow whose run-steps invoke `arch -x86_64 dart`,
/// derived per-line from [rosettaInvocations]. ...
Set<String> rosettaDartJobs(String workflowPath) =>
    rosettaInvocations(workflowPath)
        .where((inv) => inv.$3 == 'dart')
        .map((inv) => inv.$1)
        .toSet();
```

- The whole-script `scripts`/`usesRosettaDart` matcher chain is deleted; the setup-dart `architecture:` assert is factored into `hasSetupDartArchPin()` and reused.
- AC2 registers exactly the 3 expected jobs: `build-macos.yml::build-macos-cli`, `ci.yml::binaries`, `ci.yml::binaries-pr`.

## Verification (mutation check, both directions)

- Removing `architecture: ${{ matrix.arch }}` from `ci.yml::binaries` now **fails the guard**: `8 passed, 1 failed` — `ci.yml::binaries pins setup-dart architecture for its arch -x86_64 dart`. The same mutation on the shipped code stayed green, so the fix is the difference.
- Guard file after the fix: **9/9 pass** (4 AC1 + 3 AC2 jobs + 2 negative probes); `dart format --set-exit-if-changed` clean, `dart analyze` clean.

A new negative probe in the same file feeds a synthetic workflow (temp file outside `.github/workflows`) whose run script is comment-first with the invocation inside an `if` — the exact shape the old chain never saw — and asserts `rosettaDartJobs` catches it plus `hasSetupDartArchPin` is false (RED before the fix, GREEN after).

comments.body:
## Automated Code Review — REQUEST_CHANGES

**Summary**: The fa-clip fix itself is correct and verified — both Rosetta legs now pin the universal `/bin/bash` (`ci.yml:4744`, `build-macos.yml:1387`), all three `arch -x86_64 dart` jobs carry setup-dart `architecture:` pins today, and `build_fa_clip.sh` under Rosetta behaves as described. However, the new guard test's AC2 group — the half that pins the bare-`dart` exemption — never executes (start-of-string regex anchor on multi-line scripts → 0 jobs detected, 0 tests registered), so the guard ships with its documented `architecture:`-pairing contract silently unenforced.

**Key Issues**:
- ⚠️ `test/ci_2408_rosetta_interpreter_guard_test.dart:170` — AC2 dead: removing a setup-dart `architecture:` pin today stays green (details in the inline thread).
- 💡 Digest — `test/ci_2408_rosetta_interpreter_guard_test.dart:39` — matcher only sees line-leading `arch -x86_64`; compound-command forms slip past the guard (posted as a suggestion thread).
- 📝 Digest — PR description test-coverage overstatement: "a negative-probe check (a fresh `arch -x86_64 bash` violation is flagged)" — no synthetic probe exists; the only negative assertion is the regression pin's `isNot` on the fixed fa-clip strings.
- 📝 Digest — PR description opens with `Closes #2408` while its own Notes say "No Fixes/Closes keywords per repo policy" and ticket gh-2408 says the issue "closes manually when the ref goes green" — GitHub will auto-close the issue on merge regardless of green ref; drop the keyword line.

**Next Steps**:
1. Make AC2 derive its job set from `rosettaInvocations()` (per-line matching) instead of `hasMatch` on whole scripts — then removing an `architecture:` pin turns the guard red.
2. Optionally widen the guard regex to non-line-leading forms.
3. Drop the `Closes #2408` line / fix the negative-probe claim in the PR description.

## Automated Code Review — REQUEST_CHANGES (re-review round 2)

**Summary**: Round 1's findings are verifiably fixed — AC2 now derives its job set per-line via `rosettaDartJobs()` (registers the 3 real `arch -x86_64 dart` jobs; a missing `architecture:` pin fails the guard), the matcher is deliberately unanchored with a compound-command negative probe, guard 9/9 + workflow-shape family green. However the new merge of `origin/main` (`0547ef5`) resolved the CHANGELOG conflict by keeping the branch's stale file, so the PR diff now **deletes** main's `feat(2394)` Compaction 2.0 v2.1 and `fix(2404)` `## Unreleased` entries — silent release-notes loss on the curated-only CHANGELOG once merged.

**Key Issues**:
- 🚨 `CHANGELOG.md:16` — merge resolution dropped main's gh-2394/gh-2404 entries (evidence: `git diff origin/main...HEAD -- CHANGELOG.md` shows them as removals; no gate covers content). Fix: `git checkout origin/main -- CHANGELOG.md` + re-add the gh-2408 block on top.
- ✅ Registry F1 (⚠️ AC2 guard never ran) — **fixed**: per-line derivation, 3 AC2 job tests registered, comment-first/no-pin negative probe green.
- ✅ Registry F2 (💡 matcher line-leading only) — **fixed**: unanchored `RegExp(r'arch -x86_64 (\S+)')`, compound-command probe green; the optional composite-scan half is justifiably deferred (no composite contains `arch -x86_64` today).
- ✅ Round-1 digest items addressed: PR description's negative-probe claim is now real code, the `Closes #2408` line is gone.
